summary: This code manages a logo that changes size and position based on which slide is being displayed in a presentation. When the page first loads or when you're on the title slide, the logo appears large in the top left. When you navigate to any other slide, the logo shrinks and moves to the bottom right. It does this by adding and removing CSS classes that control the styling.

explanations.7: The matches() method checks if the current slide element has an ID of 'title-slide' — it's a way to ask 'does this element match this CSS selector?'
explanations.9: [].forEach.call() is a way to loop through all elements in the list, even though querySelectorAll returns a special type that doesn't normally have a forEach method — we're borrowing the forEach method from an empty array to make it work.
explanations.22: This sets up a listener that runs once when the page finishes loading, so we can initialize the logo styling and set up listeners for later slide changes.
explanations.31: Reveal.on() hooks into the presentation library (Reveal.js) to listen for whenever someone changes to a different slide, then calls our updateLogoSizePosition function.
